findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in user_data. They are exposed in Terraform state, configuration history, and potentially instance metadata/logs, allowing unauthorized AWS API access if retrieved.
TCP port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance's remote administration service to any internet host and enabling brute-force or exploitation attempts.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key. Its contents may therefore be stored unencrypted at rest, depending on account-level defaults.
The snapshot is created from a volume not configured for encryption, so it can preserve unencrypted disk contents at rest. Access to the snapshot could expose data from the attached volume.
The bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so VPC flow-log objects may be stored without bucket-enforced encryption at rest.

This separately created ENI has no security_groups specified. In a non-default VPC it uses the default security group, whose rules are not controlled by this configuration; this can unintentionally expose or overly trust traffic if that group is permissive.
